Archeage viewership crash: Numbers for the game inflated by 1100
I wanted to try Archeage when it came out in North America. Logged in, found there was no mouse inversion. Months went by without mouse inversion being added. Stopped caring about trying the game.

They had some really cool gameplay ideas that I was excited about, but as soon as I saw those insanely priced pre-release packs my heart sank. Clearly this was to be a shameless money grab by people who didn't care whether their players were happy or not. :(
Giving people the middle finger for months over a feature as simple as invert y is kind of a clear indication of not giving a shit about your players.
light grey text on white? lovely on the eyes.

fuckin hard to read. I'll copy the text here. Meanwhile, the remaining streamers for the game number at less than a dozen during North America Prime Time Hours. These streams struggle to break out of the double digits of concurrent viewers. The inflation of the game's overall viewership comes at a suspicious time as many veteran players exit the game in the wake of recent cash shop changes. These changes allowed players to heavily influence gameplay advantage in what many would consider as Pay-to-Win (P2W). Coupled with two major economy shattering bugs that allowed players to bypass the Random Number Generated (RNG) upgrade system get to the peak of end game weaponry and armor, the game community has suffered the biggest losses of active players since the changes to content in version 1.2 and the builds that came during the second half of 2014. Those changes caused, what I call, the Archeage Streamer Crash.

Read More about the feeling of that time at Engadget and at MMOBomb

At its peak in the streaming community of Archeage, there were some very influential streamers that provided the majority of the streaming content of Archeage. SxyHxy (pronounced Sexy Hexy), before being found by Team2G and becoming better known for his H1Z1 gameplay, with a background in Radio, was primarily an Archeage streamer known for his top tier gameplay in the game's one versus one (1v1) arena. At his peak, before the 1.2 builds of the 4th quarter of 2014, he averaged around 500 to 600 concurrent viewers, while after those changes he suffered a sharp drop to 200 to 300 viewership. Having left long before recent Archeage changes, SxyHxy has built his stream up to an average 800 to 1000 concurrent viewers.

Other streamers that took longer to change from Archeage suffered loses close to the same 50% reduction. Two notable cases with contrasting results are that of former AAA baseball player Pace and the comedy driven Et_Talon, the later having once lead his guild to upgrade a Tuna club to "Celestial", an expensive level upgrade that includes a server wide notification in-game of its creation. Pace has since gone back to his pre-streaming roots of Star Wars: The Old Republic , where he was formerly a Rank 1 player in that games 4v4 arena and has built his numbers back up to be within reach of his peak numbers in Archeage.

In contrast, ET_Talon has struggled to find his niche as he pursues to climb the ranks of the CS:GO competitive community and has taken a few months off due to moving his place of residence. At some points, each discussed a possible return to Archeage, but after the recent cash shop changes and bugs, the game has become the furthest from their minds for streaming.

Recent polling of MMO viewership rankings conducted in an attempt to create content for that community resulted in the discovery that the game listing for Archeage is being inflated by 1,100+ viewers over the actual numbers of live streams causing their ranking to be higher in the Twitch game listings.

Listing in Twitch streaming is very important. Twitch currently holds a laughably large majority share of the video game streaming content, so being discovered on this platform is very important for streamers, to make earnings from partnership and donations from viewers, and to publishers of video games that look to leverage the power of a content creating community. This indirect marketing source has been highly successful for publishers like Riot Games, Valve, and Blizzard as many flock to their competitive streams and then to the games themselves.

I rent all the time for work. Here are a few things i have learned over the past year.

  • Always say no to their gas offer. Youre paying for a full tank wether you used it or not. Its ONLY worth it if you plan on running the rental to empty before returning it

  • The damage liability waiver is per day and will cost you the most. If your work or insurance will cover it and your comfortable driving you can save a boat load waiving that option.

  • Find a company you like and continually rent with them. I use enterprise because theyre up front about how much its going to cost you. Hertz is the worst about hidden fees and i have had two of their cars have a transmission just shit out on me while driving.

  • Most rental places at an airport are open 24 hours but their times will be shown on the website, but make sure you know if you have to take a shuttle to a rental facility or not so you arent looking around for the counter like a jackass. Follow signage that says ground transportation or if your lucky will just say "rental cars"

  • Get a window suction cup mount for your smart phone and grab the Waze app for satnav. Will save you 10 bucks a day on your rental.

  • Aim for a standard or full size and try to get one of the newer cars. They are more fuel efficent so you will be paying out less in gas.

  • Whatever you booked for, they will try to upgrade you. Its how they get graded like a gamestop employee pushing magazine subs. Its fine to upgrade, but you usually dont want to go from full to premium, thats where the giant price hike is at. The jump between the categories lower than that is usually a couple bucks a day

Generally with better circumstances, I'd suggest paying for an upgrade. The reason for this is that you can drive a pretty sweet car you might otherwise never be able to drive (ie: BMW, Nissan Z, etc). Some times you can get REALLY good deals and it might only cost you 30-40 more than a standard economy car.
• If you already have car insurance, decline the rental agency's insurance. Nearly everyone's auto insurance covers rentals, so you're likely just throwing money away. If in doubt, check your policy.
